title: Safety Readiness Checklist
description: Assesses PPE coverage, SOP completeness, hazard controls, emergency procedures, and training readiness before commencing experiments.

steps.prompt: Assess whether PPE requirements and engineering hazard controls are identified and in place for the experiments in context. Consider: chemical splash protection (face shield, gloves, lab coat), fume hood or glovebox use for volatile or air-sensitive electrolytes, grounding for high-voltage setups, and secondary containment for liquid electrolytes. Use this rubric — 1: all PPE and controls identified, documented, and verified available; 2: minor gap (one PPE item not explicitly mentioned, low-hazard context); 3: a significant PPE item or engineering control is unaddressed for a moderate-hazard operation; 4: multiple hazard controls absent for a high-hazard experiment; 5: PPE and controls are not documented at all for a hazardous procedure. Cite specific experiment parameters or page notes. List 3-5 actionable mitigations.

Evaluate whether a complete, current Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) exists and is referenced for each non-trivial experimental step. Consider: whether SOPs are linked in experiment records or iteration pages, whether they cover the specific chemistry and equipment in use, and whether any custom or novel procedures are documented. Use this rubric — 1: SOPs present, current, and referenced for all procedures; 2: SOPs present but not explicitly referenced in records; 3: SOPs exist for standard steps but a novel or modified procedure lacks documentation; 4: SOPs largely absent, procedures described only in informal notes; 5: no SOPs and no procedure documentation. Cite evidence from the provided context. Provide 3-5 mitigations.

Determine whether emergency response procedures are established for the likely failure modes of the experiments in context. Consider: electrolyte spill response, thermal event / fire response for battery cells, emergency shutdown of high-voltage equipment, first-aid for chemical exposure, and whether emergency contacts and eyewash / safety shower locations are known. Use this rubric — 1: all emergency procedures documented and communicated; 2: standard emergency procedures in place, experiment-specific additions minor; 3: emergency procedures exist generically but not tailored to the specific hazards in these experiments; 4: emergency procedures not referenced or likely unfamiliar to operator; 5: no emergency procedures identified. Cite specific hazards from the experiment context. List 3-5 targeted mitigations.

Assess whether operator training is current and adequate for the techniques and equipment in the experiment context. Consider: whether training records are referenced, whether the operator has prior runs of the same protocol visible in the experiment history, whether any new technique or instrument is being used for the first time without a supervised trial run noted. Use this rubric — 1: training current, operator has demonstrated competency on this protocol; 2: trained on similar technique, minor extension; 3: operator appears new to a specific instrument or reagent class without documented training; 4: no training evidence for a hazardous or complex procedure; 5: operator training completely undocumented for the experiment type. Cite any training references or lack thereof. Provide 3-5 mitigations.
